rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in housing
rules.quote: It shall be unlawful: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.summary: It is unlawful for a housing owner to discriminate against or harass any person because of their source of income.
rules.effective_date_evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)

rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income inquiries in advertising
rules.quote: For any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a housing accommodation that indicates any preference, limitation, or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information or an intention to make that preference, limitation, or discrimination.
rules.summary: It is unlawful to publish any advertisement for housing that indicates a preference, limitation, or discrimination based on source of income.
rules.effective_date_evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)

rules.title: Income standards must be based on tenant-paid portion of rent for subsidized tenants
rules.quote: In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.summary: For tenants with government rent subsidies, landlords must base income standards on the portion of rent the tenant will pay, not the total rent.
rules.effective_date_evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)
rules.coverage_text: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy

rules.title: Alternative evidence for credit history for subsidized tenants
rules.quote: Use a person's credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant's discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant's reasonable ability to pay the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.
rules.summary: When using credit history to screen subsidized tenants, landlords must offer applicants the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay, such as government benefit payments, pay records, or bank statements.
rules.effective_date_evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)
rules.coverage_text: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy and landlord uses credit history in screening

rules.title: Definition of source of income includes government housing subsidies
rules.quote: For the purposes of this section, "source of income" means lawful, verifiable income paid directly to a tenant, or to a representative of a tenant, or paid to a housing owner or landlord on behalf of a tenant, including federal, state, or local public assistance, and federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including, but not limited to, federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 1437f).
rules.summary: Source of income includes lawful, verifiable income such as public assistance and housing subsidies, including Section 8 vouchers, paid to or on behalf of a tenant.
rules.effective_date_evidence: (Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, Sec. 1.   (SB 267)   Effective January 1, 2024.)
